title: Protocol for optical clearing and imaging of fluorescently labeled ex vivo rat brain slices
protocol: Autoclave all surgical instruments and materials before use.
Wear protective gloves, safety goggles, protective clothing, and a face mask.
Clean all surfaces including benchtop, vibratome, buffer tray, and tubing system with water and then 70% ethanol.
Submerge the razor blade in 70% ethanol and let it dry for 5 min.
Insert the razor blade into the blade holder and turn the vibratome on.
Check the blade’s position using VibroCheck.
Install the double-walled buffer tray.
Use a silicone tube to connect a gas diffuser to the cylinder of compressed carbogen.
Turn on the cooling unit connected to the buffer tray and set it up to 3°C at least 10 min before starting the preparation.
Fill the buffer tray with 300 ml of pre-chilled NMDG-HEPES aCSF solution.
Maintain the buffer tray with low carbogen bubbling.
Place the vibratome’s specimen plate on the benchtop next to the vibratome.
Position a straight forceps, Moria perforated spoon, glass petri dish, single Whatman round filter paper, liquid super glue, and one razor blade on the benchtop near the vibratome.
Add 80 mL of pre-chilled NMDG-HEPES aCSF solution into a 100 mL beaker.
Place the beaker inside a bucket with ice and continue carbogen bubbling using a small micro-filter-candle.
Prepare 50 mL of wash buffer and keep it in continuous carbogen bubbling using a micro-filter-candle.
Decapitate the animal with a rodent guillotine following depth anesthesia with an intraperitoneal injection of pentobarbital sodium (30–50 mg/kg).
Remove the skin of the scalp using straight sharp-blunt scissors.
Make a 1 cm lateral/ventral incision cutting both sides of basioccipital bone through the foramen magnum at the occipital bone with straight sharp-blunt scissors.
Insert scissors into the foramen magnum and cut dorsally along the middle line of the interparietal, parietal, and frontal bones until reaching the nasal bone.
Cut the nasal bone transversally at the level of the premaxilla using Mayo-Noble scissors.
Remove the nasal, frontal, parietal, and interparietal bones on both sides starting from the rostral towards the caudal direction to expose the brain.
Rinse the brain with 10 mL of pre-chilled NMDG-HEPES aCSF saturated with carbogen.
Gently scoop out the intact brain into the beaker prepared in step 2a using a long-round tip spatula.
Take the brain with a Moria perforated spoon.
Place the brain on a Whatman round filter paper in a 100 × 15 mm glass petri dish to prepare a tissue block.
Remove the olfactory bulb and cerebellum from the brain.
Glue the prepared brain vertically onto a specimen plate using liquid super glue.
Transfer the specimen plate into a buffer tray filled with chilled NMDG-HEPES aCSF continuously saturated with carbogen.
Set up the vibratome control panel to 0.14 mm/s speed, 1.10 mm amplitude, and 275 μm slice thickness.
Start sectioning from the ventral part towards the dorsal part of the brain.
Wear safety goggles during the procedure to avoid accidents with bone shards.
Prepare the tissue block within 30 seconds to maintain slice quality.
Transfer the brain slices from the vibratome’s buffer tray to a petri dish containing oxygenated pre-chilled wash buffer using a paintbrush n°6.
Rinse the brain slices twice with fresh wash buffer equilibrated at physiological temperature (37°C).
Organize 6-well culture plate, Millicell culture inserts, autoclaved cover glass forceps and paintbrush n°6 for quick access.
Clean the brush with 70% ethanol, let it dry for 5 min and rinse with deionized water thoroughly.
Add 1 ml of brain slice culture medium to each well of a 6-well culture plate.
Place a Millicell culture insert into each well using flat cover glass forceps.
Add an additional 0.5 ml of slice culture media on top of each insert.
Place the 6-well culture plate in the incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2 for at least 30 min to pre-warm the culture medium.
Manually transfer individual brain slices to each culture insert in a 6-well culture plate using a paintbrush number 6.
Carefully perform the step to avoid damaging the tissue.
Return the 6-well culture plate containing the brain slices in culture medium to the 37°C incubator with 5% CO2.
Ensure no areas of the brain slices are folded or wrinkled.
Every second day, remove approximately 1 mL of culture medium from the bottom of each well and the excess medium that collects in the Millicell culture insert without disturbing the brain slice.
Add 1 mL of fresh and pre-warmed culture medium to the bottom of each well.
Add an additional 0.3 mL of fresh and pre-warmed culture medium inside the Millicell culture insert to submerge the brain slice.
Maintain brain slices in culture as long as required by the experimental plan.
Equilibrate the culture medium at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 30 min before transferring brain slices and before every medium change.
Transfer an entire rat coronal brain slice per Millicell culture insert or transfer 1-2 coronal brain slices-separated hemispheres depending on experimental conditions.
Avoid overlapping brain slices in the Millicell culture insert and ensure slices do not contact the sides of the insert.
Use a paintbrush to transfer 275 μm thick brain slices if they are not disturbed by this method.
Alternatively, use an inverted glass Pasteur pipette to position individual slices in each Millicell culture insert.
Remove excess wash buffer immediately after transferring brain slices with fresh and pre-warmed culture media.
Remove the culture medium and add 1 mL of 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) solution pH 7.4 into the well.
Add an additional 1 mL PFA on top of the brain slice and fix for 20 min at room temperature (20°C–23°C).
Gently transfer each fixed brain slice from the Millicell culture insert to a glass vial with lid containing 1 mL KPBS using a paintbrush.
Wash the slice 2 × 5 min with KPBS at room temperature (20°C–23°C) by adding 1 mL of KPBS per vial.
Remove the KPBS from each vial.
Permeabilize and block the brain slice by adding 1 mL of blocking solution in each vial.
Incubate overnight at room temperature (20°C–23°C), or at 4°C for two days.
Prepare the primary antibody solution diluted (for this experiment rabbit anti-Iba1, 1:1000) in 1 mL of blocking solution.
Remove blocking solution from the glass vial containing the brain slice.
Add 1 mL of primary antibody solution.
Incubate at room temperature (20°C–23°C) for 48–72 hours.
Remove the primary antibody solution.
Wash the sample with KPBS 3 times, each for 20 minutes, on a shaking platform at mild speed (100 RPM).
Prepare secondary antibody solution diluted 1:200 in 1 mL of blocking solution and add DAPI (1:1000) for nuclear stain.
Protect secondary antibody solution from light during preparation.
Remove KPBS from the glass vial containing the brain slice.
Add 1 mL of secondary antibody solution.
Incubate at room temperature (20°C–23°C) for 24–48 hours.
Remove the secondary antibody solution.
Wash the sample with KPBS 3 times, each for 20 minutes, on a shaking platform at mild speed (100 RPM).
Dehydrate brain slices in methanol.
Prepare the methanol series (20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100%).
Remove KPBS from the glass vial containing the brain slice.
Add 1 ml of 20% methanol and incubate for 10 min at room temperature on a shaking platform at mild speed.
Remove the 20% methanol solution and add 1 ml 40% methanol. Incubate for 10 min at room temperature on a shaking platform at mild speed.
Remove the 40% methanol solution and add 1 ml 60% methanol. Incubate for 10 min at room temperature on a shaking platform at mild speed.
Remove the 60% methanol solution and add 1 ml 80% methanol. Incubate for 10 min at room temperature on a shaking platform at mild speed.
Remove the methanol solution.
Add 1 mL of 100% methanol.
Incubate for 10 min at room temperature (20°C–23°C) on a shaking platform at mild speed (100 RPM).
Remove the methanol solution.
Add 1 mL of DCM/methanol mixture solution.
Incubate for 1 h at room temperature (20°C–23°C) on a shaking platform at mild speed (100 RPM).
Remove the DCM/methanol mixture solution.
Add 1 mL of DCM.
Incubate for 10 min at room temperature (20°C–23°C) on a shaking platform at mild speed (100 RPM).
Remove the DCM.
Add 1 mL of DCM.
Incubate for 10 min at room temperature (20°C–23°C) on a shaking platform at mild speed (100 RPM).
Remove the DCM from the glass vial containing the brain slice.
Add 500 μL of ethyl cinnamate per well in the black Ibidi μ-Plate 24 well plate with flat and clear bottom for high throughput microscopy.
Add 500 μL of ethyl cinnamate to avoid DCM carry-over.
Gently transfer the cleared brain slice from the glass vial to the Ibidi μ-Plate 24 well plate containing ethyl cinnamate using a paintbrush.
Incubate overnight at 4°C protected from light.
Flatten the immunostained and cleared brain slice.
Reduce the volume of ethyl cinnamate so it just covers the brain slice.
Place a round glass coverslip in the well on top of the brain slice.
Place 3–4 metal nuts on top of the coverslip to mechanically flatten the brain slice.
Image the brain slice by taking a z-stack throughout the thickness of the sample.
Correct for RI mismatch using the provided formula.
